name: Garden of Eden Trail, Apalachicola Bluffs and Ravines Preserve (Alum Bluff)
coordinateNote: Entrance or parking coordinates from the November 12, 2026 gap review.
navigationDestination: Garden of Eden Trail trailhead, Garden of Eden Road off State Road 12, 1.6 miles east of Bristol, FL 32321
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Hike 3.75 miles round trip from longleaf sandhills down a steep slope forest, across a seepage stream in a steephead ravine, and back up to the Alum Bluff overlook of the river floodplain. The ravines hold the rare Florida torreya; gopher tortoises and reintroduced eastern indigo snakes live on the preserve. Plan about 3 hours; climbs are steep.
access: Self-guided, foot traffic only. No pets, bikes, camping or fires; stay well back from the unstable bluff edge. Hunting occurs nearby November through February, so wear bright colors. Trailhead is 0.4 mile up Garden of Eden Road. Preserve contact 850-643-2756 / VisitABRP@tnc.org.

conditions.summary: TNC's preserve page reads 'OPEN TO THE PUBLIC' but still carries an old banner closing the preserve for Hurricane Helene from Sept 24, 2024, and shows no Isaias notice. Bristol is roughly 100 miles east of the Isaias landfall. Call or email the preserve before going. (source dated read 2026-11-12)

name: Porter Lake (Apalachicola National Forest)
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Primitive camping and day use with picnic tables, toilets and paddling access into the Ochlockonee floodplain; also a Florida Trail trailhead toward Bradwell Bay. It works as a hunt camp in gun season and non-hunters may still camp.
access: No reservation needed. Stay limit: 14 days per month (National Forests in Florida) Derived, not read from the 2026-27 brochure (FWC brochure app errored): rule text says general gun is 'the first 58 days of Zone D antlered deer season'; with FWC's 2026-27 Zone D dates that is Nov 26-29, 2026 and Dec 12, 2026 - Feb 3, 2027. Rule: on National Forest lands camping is 'only on designated campsites during general gun season', so on Nov 26-29 roadside dispersed camping in Apalachicola NF is not legal and a listed hunt camp or campground is the legal choice. Small game season opens the second Saturday of November outside general gun days. Orange requirement not checked; expect armed hunters in camp over Thanksgiving weekend. Forest Service: non-hunters may camp here in gun season but should 'Be aware of hunting environment'.

conditions.summary: Forest Service page shows 'Site Open', updated after Hurricane Isaias. A natural well is listed but the same page says potable water is not available. (source dated 2026-10-14)
